name: Strife
label: Victory Records
lede: Straight edge kids from Thousand Oaks got Deftones' singer, Fear Factory's guitarist and Sepultura's drummer onto one hardcore record, broke up from exhaustion, and came back no longer edge.

eras.title: Straight edge from Thousand Oaks
eras.text: Strife came out of Thousand Oaks in 1991, the Ventura County end of the Southern California straight edge scene. Two early records on New Age and a spot on a Victory Records compilation came before the first album.

years.h: Strife forms in Thousand Oaks, California
years.p: Singer Rick Rodney and guitarist Andrew Kline start a straight edge hardcore band northwest of Los Angeles.

years.h: My Fire Burns On... on New Age Records
years.p: Strife's first 7" comes out on New Age Records, the Southern California straight edge label, followed the same year by a self-titled release.

years.h: What Will Remain? on Victory's Only the Strong
years.p: Strife appears on Victory Records' 1993 compilation, catalog VR10, alongside [[Snapcase|90f7f8df-db45-4a6c-89fb-9e912f77eabd]].

eras.title: One Truth, warts and all
eras.text: One Truth put a Southern California straight edge band on Chicago's Victory Records. Strife toured it, filmed it, and shared a live record with labelmates from Syracuse and Buffalo.

years.p: Strife's debut LP is Victory Records catalog number 14. AllMusic's Greg Prato calls Strife the band that led California hardcore's charge in the early-to-mid 90s.
years.xp: AllMusic's bio says the album came out through Caroline Records before Strife signed to Victory; Wikipedia lists it as a Victory release from the start. Victory reissued it in 2006.

years.h: The Grey 7" and the One Truth Live video
years.p: Strife releases the Grey single and a home video, One Truth Live, which AllMusic says shows touring hardcore life in the 90s, warts and all.

years.h: California Takeover Live with Earth Crisis and Snapcase
years.p: Victory Records catalog 042 puts Strife's To an End and Lift on one live album with [[Earth Crisis|88a6037e-87ba-492a-a54c-c927aa620cb8]] and [[Snapcase|90f7f8df-db45-4a6c-89fb-9e912f77eabd]].

eras.title: Chino, Dino and Igor
eras.text: For its second album Strife pulled in guests from three of the era's biggest heavy bands, got its sound right, and then fell apart. Victory cleaned out the vault on the way out.

years.h: In This Defiance, with Chino Moreno, Dino Cazares and Igor Cavalera
years.p: Deftones' Chino Moreno sings on Will to Die, Fear Factory's Dino Cazares adds guitar, and Sepultura's Igor Cavalera plays extra drums. AllMusic says Strife finally hit everything just right.
years.xp: The line-up was Rick Rodney, Andrew Kline and Todd Turnham on guitars, Chad Peterson on bass and Sid Niesen on drums, with Bob Marlette mixing. Metal Hammer later ranked it seventh among the most underrated hardcore albums, and a Canadian straight edge band took its name from the record.

years.h: Blistered gets a video and goes on Hopeless's Cinema Beer Nuts
years.p: Blistered from In This Defiance becomes Strife's first music video and lands on the Hopeless Records sampler Cinema Beer Nuts.

years.h: Strife breaks up over creative differences and exhaustion
years.p: Strife calls it quits two years after In This Defiance, just as things seemed to be going well, according to AllMusic.
years.xp: AllMusic dates the breakup to early 1998; Wikipedia places it two years after the 1997 album. Either way, it came right after the band's best-received record.

years.p: Victory Records (VR092) gathers Strife's live tracks and unreleased material into one posthumous set, released after the band had split.

eras.title: Angry, and no longer edge
eras.text: Benefit shows brought Strife back, and within a year it was a band again. The comeback record dropped straight edge but kept the rage.

years.p: Strife plays several benefit concerts, a year or so after breaking up.

years.h: Angermeans: Strife is back, and no longer straight edge
years.p: Recorded at The Steakhouse in North Hollywood for Victory Records. The band calls it a more focused continuation of In This Defiance; AllMusic calls it a long-overdue kick in the butt for hardcore.
years.xp: Lyrics are Rick Rodney's, most of the music Andrew Kline's. Rock Hard gave it 8.5 out of 10. The album was followed by Strife's first major tour in nearly four years.

eras.title: A rebirth recorded partly in Brazil
eras.text: Victory reissued the catalog, and Strife kept touring far from Thousand Oaks: Japan, South America, Europe, Mexico. The next record, eleven years after the last, was produced by Terror's drummer and mixed in São Paulo.

years.h: Victory reissues One Truth, In This Defiance and Angermeans
years.p: Victory Records puts all three Strife albums back in print.
Strife and East Coast youth crew band [[Floorpunch|8ecf80c2-d090-4cbd-97ec-0a0824301041]] tour Japan together, part of a run that also took Strife through South America, Europe and Mexico.

years.h: Witness a Rebirth, produced by Terror's Nick Jett
years.p: Strife's first album in 11 years comes out on 6131 and Holy Roar. [[Terror|697eba1a-bf52-46b1-a19f-4d7190b63e5c]] drummer Nick Jett produces and drums, with Igor Cavalera and Marc Rizzo guesting, mixed at Nova Studios in São Paulo.
years.xp: Andrew Kline said it would be more along the lines of In This Defiance. Members of Terror also contributed. AllMusic and Louder both gave it 2.5 stars out of 5.

years.p: Strife releases a video for Carry the Torch, following Torn Apart in 2012.

eras.title: Andrew Kline's side roads
eras.text: Strife's guitarist kept one foot in the band and started others: a supergroup with Terror's singer and his own label, which put Strife's best record back on vinyl.

years.h: Andrew Kline and Scott Vogel start World Be Free
years.p: Kline joins [[Terror|697eba1a-bf52-46b1-a19f-4d7190b63e5c]]'s [[Scott Vogel|4ab1b4fb-f2fe-458c-a496-0de55c7bf3cb]], Sammy Siegler, Joe Garlipp and Alex Barreto in World Be Free, later on Revelation Records.

years.h: In This Defiance on vinyl, 100 copies, on WAR Records
years.p: Andrew Kline's own label WAR Records reissues the 1997 album in a 100-copy pressing. Victory reissues it again in 2020.
Strife, [[Earth Crisis|88a6037e-87ba-492a-a54c-c927aa620cb8]] and [[Snapcase|90f7f8df-db45-4a6c-89fb-9e912f77eabd]] share a record again, 25 years after the original.
